market_note: No roster change vs the June 4 list: the same AI-chip, optical-module and battery leaders top the CUS, with attention rotating harder into domestic-silicon names (Cambricon, SMIC, Hygon) after Cambricon's +21.6% single-session spike. Tape softened on geopolitics not fundamentals (Hang Seng -1.59% to ~23,925 on Jun 18; US-Iran talks scrapped, Brent toward ~$80), while A-share AI self-sufficiency earnings kept compounding.

names.name: Cambricon
names.driver: Targeting ~500k AI accelerators in 2026 (incl. up to 300k Siyuan 590/690) as China's government procurement whitelist and DeepSeek-V4 Day-0 support pull demand away from Nvidia.
names.risk: Output is gated by SMIC 7nm (N+2) capacity and ~20% large-die yields plus scarce HBM, so the volume ramp may badly undershoot guidance.
names.guide: Sell-side sees triple-digit 2026 revenue growth continuing, but flags execution/valuation risk at ~¥1,500 with the stock again China's priciest.
names.cash: Net cash positive, well funded post-2025 raise

names.name: Zhongji Innolight
names.driver: 1.6T optical-module ramp for global AI-datacenter capex drove blowout Q1 with revenue nearly tripling and management lifting a ¥1.11B cash dividend.
names.risk: Single-customer/hyperscaler-capex concentration and CPO substitution fears make the name vulnerable to any AI-capex digestion.
names.guide: Analysts model continued 1.6T mix-up through 2026; consensus stays constructive on the optical-module cycle.

names.name: CATL
names.driver: Storage doubled to ~50GWh in Q1 (guiding mix from ~20% toward ~50%) and sodium-ion Naxtra reaches GWh-scale and first storage deliveries in September.
names.risk: Beijing's anti-involution crackdown (battery price-war curbs, VAT export rebate cut 9%->6%) plus a 2 TWh national overcapacity overhang.
names.guide: Huatai sees full-year storage shipments ~225GWh (+87%); fresh HKD39.2B H-share placement funds global capacity.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: ¥129.13B, +52.5% YoY, beat (net profit +48.5% to ¥20.74B, ~33% above estimates)
names.backlog: Multi-year storage + NEV OEM supply contracts

names.name: Eoptolink
names.driver: Q1 revenue more than doubled past ¥8B on sustained AI compute demand, with ~49% gross margin as 800G/1.6T shipments scale to hyperscalers.
names.risk: FX losses dented net margin and the 'Yi-Zhong-Tian' optical cohort is prone to violent single-day drawdowns on any capex-peak narrative.
names.guide: Street expects the AI-driven optical upcycle to persist into 2026, though margin watched on FX and mix.

names.name: Foxconn Industrial Internet
names.driver: AI-server revenue surged ~30%+ to overtake iPhones, with AI GPU-rack and ASIC-server shipments doubling Q1 profit as it gains hyperscaler share.
names.risk: Thin ODM margins and dependence on a few cloud customers leave it exposed to any AI-capex air-pocket or rack-mix shift.
names.guide: Management/Street bullish on 2026 AI-server demand (TrendForce sees +28% global shipments); 2025 revenue topped ¥900B.

names.name: Hygon
names.driver: 'Dual-chip' CPU+DCU strategy and DeepSeek-V4 Day-0 support are driving sharp government/internet/finance DCU adoption, with Q1 revenue guided +63-76%.
names.risk: The flagship Sugon absorption merger reportedly collapsed/stalled (Dec-2025), clouding the consolidation thesis, and it shares SMIC capacity constraints.
names.guide: Analysts see 2026 DCU demand accelerating; 128-core accelerators slated across supercomputing centers by Q3-2026.

names.name: SMIC
names.driver: Q2 guided revenue +14-16% with margins to 20-22% on AI-driven demand and price hikes, while 7nm capacity is reportedly set to double in 2026 (key Cambricon/Huawei supplier).
names.risk: As the chokepoint for China's entire AI-silicon ramp, equipment/export controls and DUV-based 7nm yield limits cap output and earnings.
names.guide: Management guides strong sequential Q2 growth and rising utilization (93%); seen as the structural beneficiary of domestic-AI demand.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: $2.505B revenue, +0.7% QoQ, in line (GM 20.1%, +0.9pp; net profit +0.4%)
names.cash: Strong; heavy capex on capacity build

names.name: GigaDevice
names.driver: Tight supply and rising prices across DRAM, NOR flash and SLC NAND drove Q1 revenue +120% and net profit ~5.1x on recovering AI/server/industrial demand.
names.risk: Memory is deeply cyclical, so any pricing roll-over or demand wobble would compress the just-recovered margins quickly.
names.guide: Company sees niche DRAM and NAND prices rising through 2026; HK-listed shares up ~3.4x YTD on the upcycle.
names.backlog: Order visibility strong on tight memory supply

names.name: Tianfu Communication
names.driver: AI-datacenter demand for high-speed optical devices is driving Q1 net profit up an estimated 95-108% YoY, with active+passive product lines and smart-manufacturing efficiency gains.
names.risk: Smaller, component-level player highly levered to the same hyperscaler optical-capex cycle and CPO transition risk.
names.guide: Analysts stay positive on optical-component demand into 2026 on continued global data-center buildout.

names.name: BYD
names.driver: May NEVs broke an 8-month decline (~383k wholesale) on record overseas volume (160k, +80%), shifting mix toward higher-margin exports.
names.risk: Brutal domestic NEV price war (Xiaomi/Geely) plus anti-involution scrutiny crushed Q1 profit -55% and keeps per-unit margins under pressure.
names.guide: Analysts expect overseas growth to cushion weak domestic unit economics; profitability recovery hinges on price-war de-escalation.
names.cash: Strong balance sheet; large operating cash base
